text:
Tool: workspace_list
Purpose: List files and directories in the project currently open in FrustIDE.
When to use: Use before assuming the project layout or choosing a file to inspect.
Minimum access: OBSERVE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"limit":{"default":200,"maximum":1000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"path":{"default":".","description":"Path relative to the open project.","type":"string"},"recursive":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_list

text:
Tool: workspace_read
Purpose: Read a UTF-8 project file with line numbers and optional line bounds.
When to use: Read specifications and surrounding source before proposing or making an edit.
Minimum access: OBSERVE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"end_line":{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"path":{"description":"Path relative to the open project.","type":"string"},"start_line":{"default":1,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":["path"],"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_read

text:
Tool: workspace_search
Purpose: Search UTF-8 text files in the open project and return matching paths, lines, and excerpts.
When to use: Use to find definitions, references, requirements, and relevant documentation before editing.
Minimum access: OBSERVE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"file_pattern":{"default":"*","type":"string"},"limit":{"default":50,"maximum":200,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"path":{"default":".","description":"Path relative to the open project.","type":"string"},"query":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}},"required":["query"],"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_search

text:
Tool: registry_search
Purpose: List or search the public Frate pod registry and return published pod metadata and exports.
When to use: Use before inventing a dependency or asking the user which pods exist. An empty query lists all published pods; a query filters pod names by substring.
Minimum access: OBSERVE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"limit":{"default":25,"maximum":100,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"query":{"default":"","description":"Optional case-insensitive pod-name substring. Empty lists all pods.","type":"string"}},"type":"object"}
title: Use registry_search

text:
Tool: workspace_create_directory
Purpose: Create a directory inside the project currently open in FrustIDE, including missing parents.
When to use: Use to establish a requested project or module layout. It succeeds when the directory already exists.
Minimum access: WORKSPACE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"path":{"description":"Path relative to the open project.","type":"string"}},"required":["path"],"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_create_directory

text:
Tool: workspace_create_file
Purpose: Create a new UTF-8 source, specification, or documentation file without overwriting an existing file.
When to use: Use for new files. If the file exists, read it and make a focused edit instead.
Minimum access: WORKSPACE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"content":{"type":"string"},"path":{"description":"Path relative to the open project.","type":"string"}},"required":["path","content"],"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_create_file

text:
Tool: workspace_write_file
Purpose: Rewrite the complete contents of an existing UTF-8 project file using an optimistic revision check.
When to use: Use after reading the file when a full-file repair is safer than a sequence of exact replacements. Pass the SHA-256 value returned by workspace_read; the write is rejected if the file changed afterward.
Minimum access: WORKSPACE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"content":{"type":"string"},"expected_sha256":{"description":"SHA-256 revision returned by the most recent workspace_read of this file.","pattern":"^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$","type":"string"},"path":{"description":"Path relative to the open project.","type":"string"}},"required":["path","content","expected_sha256"],"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_write_file

text:
Tool: workspace_replace_text
Purpose: Replace exact text in an existing UTF-8 project file.
When to use: Use for focused edits after reading the file. By default the old text must occur exactly once.
Minimum access: WORKSPACE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"new_text":{"type":"string"},"old_text":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"path":{"description":"Path relative to the open project.","type":"string"},"replace_all":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["path","old_text","new_text"],"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_replace_text

text:
Tool: workspace_check_frust
Purpose: Compile-check a Frust source file directly from project content and return structured compiler diagnostics without creating temporary files.
When to use: Use after editing Frust code. Fix reported errors and repeat until the check passes before completing the task.
Minimum access: OBSERVE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"path":{"description":"Frust source path relative to the open project.","type":"string"}},"required":["path"],"type":"object"}
title: Use workspace_check_frust

text:
Tool: run_command
Purpose: Run a command in PowerShell inside the open project: compile, build and test any language (C++ with CMake or MSBuild, C# and F# with dotnet, Rust with cargo, Frust with frate), run a script, or look at the project with git. The host judges every command first: some run at once, some are shown to the user to approve, some are refused with the reason. It returns the exit code and the output (the start and the end of long output, with the full log kept).
When to use: Use it to build and test after changing code in any language other than Frust, and repair what the compiler reports until the build and tests pass. On this machine builds are single-core and name their target: use 'cmake --build <dir> --config Debug --target <name>', 'msbuild <project> /t:<target> /p:Configuration=Debug' (never /m), and 'dotnet build' or 'dotnet test' (the host adds -m:1). Never build or install LLVM and never run vcpkg install. A program that waits for input or keeps running (a REPL, a server, a game) never finishes here, because this shell has no keyboard or screen: open it with launch_program instead. Say in 'reason' what the command is for, so the user can decide quickly. If the user does not allow a command, do not try to get around it; ask with agent_request_user.
Minimum access: WORKSPACE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"command":{"description":"The PowerShell command to run.","type":"string"},"cwd":{"description":"The folder to run it in, relative to the open project. Default: the project root.","type":"string"},"reason":{"description":"What the command is for, in a sentence the user can read.","type":"string"},"timeout_seconds":{"description":"Stop it after this long. Default 120, or 900 for a build or test.","maximum":1800,"minimum":5,"type":"integer"}},"required":["command","reason"],"type":"object"}
title: Use run_command

text:
Tool: launch_program
Purpose: Open a program in its own visible window on the user's screen, the way the user would start it, and return at once: a console program (a REPL, a text game, a menu) gets its own console the user can type into; a windowed app shows its window. Use this, not run_command, for anything that waits for input or keeps running. The user is asked first.
When to use: Use when the user wants to try the program, or when it is interactive or long-running (a REPL, a server, a game). Give the command that starts it, for example 'dotnet run' or '.\bin\Debug\net9.0\App.exe', and the folder. You cannot see the window: ask the user what it shows (agent_request_user), or check behaviour with builds and tests. Close it with stop_program when it is no longer needed.
Minimum access: WORKSPACE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"command":{"description":"The PowerShell command that starts the program.","type":"string"},"cwd":{"description":"The folder to start it in, relative to the open project. Default: the project root.","type":"string"},"reason":{"description":"Why the user should see it, in a sentence.","type":"string"}},"required":["command","reason"],"type":"object"}
title: Use launch_program

text:
Tool: stop_program
Purpose: Close a program opened with launch_program (and everything it started), or with no process_id, list the ones still running.
When to use: Use when a program you opened is no longer needed, or before rebuilding it (a running program can lock its own files).
Minimum access: WORKSPACE.
Arguments schema: {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"process_id":{"description":"The process id launch_program reported. Leave out to list what is running.","type":"integer"}},"type":"object"}
title: Use stop_program
